NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)  
To prevent/mitigate series string imbalance drift in a 13-cell NMC-811 lithium-ion battery module under a 15°C top-to-bottom thermal gradient, I propose adding a thermal shunt array between cell tabs to equalize temperature-driven self-discharge variation. Standard practice relies solely on active balancing (1 A current) to correct voltage spreads; this intervention introduces passive thermal conduction to reduce the driving mechanism (thermal gradient-induced self-discharge mismatch) without altering cell chemistry or active balancing. The closest existing practice is thermal management in EV battery packs, but those use active cooling/heating or phase-change materials, whereas this uses a bilayer shunt stack of pure copper (high thermal conductivity) and polyimide (electrical insulation) to conduct heat between adjacent cells while blocking electrical current. The mechanism attacks the failure by reducing ΔT across cells, thereby lowering self-discharge rate divergence.

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Self-discharge rate mismatch ΔSD ∝ exp(Ea/kT) × ΔT, where Ea is activation energy, k is Boltzmann’s constant, and T is temperature. A 15°C gradient induces ~10% ΔSD variation between top and bottom cells at 25°C average. The shunt array reduces ΔT by 80% (from 15°C to 3°C), cutting ΔSD to ~2%. This reduces the voltage spread driver (ΔV = ΔSD × t) by 8× over time, keeping ΔV < 35 mV at rest. DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = ΔT; the mechanism moves it DOWN by 12°C via thermal shunting; this REDUCES the failure driver (self-discharge rate divergence).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
Standard practice: Active balancing only (1 A current).  
Intervention additions:  
- (b) Pure copper shunt strip, 0.1 mm thick × 5 mm wide (stock electrical busbar grade), bonded between adjacent cell tabs using the module’s existing ultrasonic welder (no new equipment).  
- (b) Polyimide insulating film, 25 μm thick (standard Kapton HN grade), laminated onto copper shunt via the module’s existing lamination process (no new equipment).  
- (c) Duty change: Activate thermal shunting during rest periods (balancer idle state) to maximize heat transfer without energy penalty.  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installation: Same as standard (shunts added during module assembly; no extra steps).  
- Commissioning: Zero (passive, no calibration needed).  
- Operation: Same energy use (shunts conduct heat only; no current draw).  
- Maintenance: Same (shunts are solid-state, no consumables).  
- Operational loss: Zero (shunting occurs during rest periods, not production).  
Parity: Same burden class (all rows use existing infrastructure or catalog parts).  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Assemble 4 modules (2 control, 2 intervention) with thermal shunts. Cycle at 1C charge/discharge (25°C to 40°C) for 1,000 cycles. Measure ΔV at rest after each cycle.  
Instruments: Existing BMS voltage sensors, thermocouples at each cell.  
Pass/fail: Intervention modules maintain ΔV < 35 mV; control modules exceed 35 mV by cycle 500.  
Duration: 1,000 cycles (~6 months at 1C).  
Kill criterion: If ΔV > 35 mV in any intervention module by cycle 200, fail.  

MECHANISM CLASS: Thermal shunt array.

- Operation: Same energy use (shunts conduct heat only; no current draw).
- Maintenance: Same (shunts are solid-state, no consumables).
